notes.dram_banks: OBSERVED on the phone (run oriole-probe1 (2026-11-12, probe shim git 36cacae, image sha256 981284da), capture device/google/oriole/hardware/probe-log-2026-11-12-oriole-probe1.txt): /memory banks 0x80000000, 0x880000000, 0x900000000, 0x980000000, 2 GiB each; the high three are contiguous and merged here; no reserved range lies above 0x880000000. notes.xnu_ram: Deliberately the same 4 GiB window as bluejay (the XNU memory path is observed only with this size); it must lie inside a hole-free bank with no reserved range inside. Growing it to 6 GiB is a later, separate change.
notes.aoc_carveout: OBSERVED in the stock recovery capture oriole-ref1 (~/pixelios-artifacts/ref/oriole/20261114T072643Z): dmesg:21 reserved memory aoc@94000000, 49152 KiB, nomap; iomem.txt:186-187 '94000000-96ffffff : 19000000.aoc' inside '93000000-973fffff : reserved'; dmesg:2067 'found aoc ... dram:[mem 0x94000000-0x96ffffff]'. Read from source: memory-region = <&aoc_reserve> (Google devices/google/gs101 a9b5edb gs101-aoc.dtsi:48); the AOC image body goes to its base and the GSA locks it (kernel/google-modules/soc/gs include/linux/gsa/gsa_aoc.h:26-41), docs/research/50 sections 5-6, 8. It lies in the low DRAM bank, outside xnu_ram, so XNU never allocates it (tools/test_aoc_carveout.py); XNU code that touches it maps it itself.

notes.fg: read from source, raviole wiring of the MAX77759 fuel gauge (ModelGauge m5) for the opt-in XNU reader of xnu patch old-oriole-0148 (boot-arg sweetbatt=1, bsd/dev/sweet_hsi2c_fg.h: READ transfers only; the same controller sequence as the shim --fg-read of branch wip/shim-fg-read, shim/fgread.c, reviewed docs/reviews/fgread-review-fable-1.md there). Feeds the ADT node /sweet-batt (tools/mkadt.py). VDT = Google devices/google/gs101 a9b5edb (~/.hermes/cache/scratch/src-dev-gs101), BMS = Google kernel/google-modules/bms 183509a (~/.hermes/cache/scratch/src-gm-bms), GKI = kernel/common android-gs-raviole-6.1-android16 a4662a84 (ios-pixel6/pixel6-oriole-kernel). bus i2c12 + addr7 0x36: VDT dts/gs101-raviole-battery.dtsi:150-155 (&hsi2c_12, clock-frequency 400000), :182-185 (max77759fg@36, compatible maxim,max77759, reg <0x36>), included for oriole through Google devices/google/raviole 81506b9 dts/gs101-oriole.dtsi:8 -> gs101-oriole-common.dtsi:8 -> gs101-raviole.dtsi:10 (oriole data: gs101-oriole-battery.dtsi:13-17); gauge-type 2 (:192) = MAX_M5_GAUGE_TYPE (BMS maxfg_common.h:19). rsense_10uohm 500 = maxim,rsense-default (VDT :193), units of 10 uOhm (BMS max1720x_battery.c:473-477), i.e. 5 mOhm. regs (the ONLY registers the reader reads, in this order; tools/mkadt.py and the patch header pin the list): RepSOC 0x06, Temp 0x08, VCell 0x09, Current 0x0A, AvgCurrent 0x0B, FullCapRep 0x35, DevName 0x21 (BMS max_m5_reg.h:209,219,224,229,234,894,548); all inside the plain readable range 0x00..0x4F of max_m5_is_reg (BMS max_m5.c:1592-1596; the same predicate is the regmap volatile_reg, :1621). The shim --fg-read read five of them (not Current and DevName). Access: regmap reg_bits 8, val_bits 16, REGMAP_ENDIAN_NATIVE (BMS max_m5.c:1615-1618, map created on the 0x36 client, :1677) = one register byte written, then two data bytes read with a repeated start (GKI drivers/base/regmap/regmap-i2c.c:172-198, two messages in one i2c_transfer), LSB first (guess: NATIVE on little-endian arm64; consistent with the values of run oriole-fg1, observed). Units: VCell 78.125 uV/LSB (BMS maxfg_common.h:192-196), RepSOC 1/256 % (:210-214), Temp 1/256 degC signed (:198-202), Current / AvgCurrent s16 * 156250 / rsense uA (max1720x_battery.c:473-477; Linux reports the negative as current_now / current_avg, :1147,1152; the reader prints the register sign). FullCapRep, Current and DevName are printed raw. Also on hsi2c_12 and NEVER addressed: 0x66 MAX77759 PMIC (VDT :158-161), 0x69 MAX77759 charger (:208-211), 0x25 MAX77759 TCPC (VDT gs101-common-typec.dtsi:103-107), 0x57 PCA9468 (raviole gs101-raviole-charging.dtsi:94-101), 0x35 MAX20339 OVP (VDT gs101-common-typec.dtsi:83-90; 0x35 is also the FullCapRep REGISTER number, sent only as the pointer byte to 0x36). handoff = the HSI2C12 words the bootloader leaves, OBSERVED on the phone in run oriole-peri1 (2026-11-14, READ-ONLY --peri-probe, all nine) and again in run oriole-fg1 (2026-11-14, --fg-read: the eight it prints; restore=ok to the same values); the XNU reader refuses unless the live controller holds exactly these (it runs much later than the shim), so its restore values are always these.
